{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "josibake",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Strong Concept ACK endorsing in-house customizable test runner"
    },
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objected to fallback printing type names instead of compile failure on unprintable types (resolved with static assert and CHECK_NO_DISPLAY)"
    },
    {
      "login": "fanquake",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "clarified Boost header-only usage and discussed constexpr / inline constexpr sweeps"
    },
    {
      "login": "jeanpablojp",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK, but raised multiple behavioral regressions and bug reports (resolved by author pushes)"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:3571556207",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "Silently printing mangled or compile-time type names at runtime instead of failing compilation when formatting is missing loses compile-time safety and differs from master.",
      "quote": "This should remain a compile failure, like it is on current master.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3577755372",
        "rc:3578111730",
        "rc:3579556440",
        "rc:3588808596",
        "rc:3614281814"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3595340862",
      "settled_by_quote": "CHECK_NO_DISPLAY sounds fine. The benefit of the static assert is that it can print the problem and solution at compile time"
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5061768134",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Dropping BOOST_TEST_RUN_FILTERS causes test coverage scripts to run the whole test suite instead of specific suites, and dropping flags breaks downstream scripts like libmultiprocess CI.",
      "quote": "BOOST_TEST_RUN_FILTERS is no longer read, so deterministic-unittest-coverage runs the whole binary instead of the suite it was given.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5618550287"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "c:5618550287",
      "settled_by_quote": "I added a catch_system_error flag for compatibility as well as a separation between the summary and log level."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390075",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Comparing null C-strings segfaults rather than reporting a test failure.",
      "quote": "With either side null this segfaults instead of reporting the failure.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978611293"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3978611293",
      "settled_by_quote": "Added a check if either side is null so it does not go through strcmp"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390077",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Unflushed output causes test logs before a crash to be lost and causes duplicate output on child process exits.",
      "quote": "This never flushes. With a crash inside a test case and output redirected, master keeps the preceding lines and here the file comes back empty.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978604713"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3978604713",
      "settled_by_quote": "I think a cout flush should solve these. Updated in latest push."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390078",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "Dropping the entire guix linker block drops -Wl,--fatal-warnings from all Linux builds instead of only dropping the riscv64 exception.",
      "quote": "Dropping the whole block means no Linux host links with -Wl,--fatal-warnings any more, while build_win.sh and build_win_gui.sh keep it.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978584583"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3978584583",
      "settled_by_quote": "Added Wl, --fatal-warnings on head commit, lmk if thats what you mean"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390082",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "BOOST_TEST_RANDOM is treated as a boolean without parsing the seed value or logging the used seed, making test run ordering non-reproducible.",
      "quote": "Here the value is only checked for presence, never read, so 0 and an empty string both turn shuffling on and a fixed seed no longer reproduces.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978594424"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3978594424",
      "settled_by_quote": "Fixed by using a random seed and printing it if equal to 1, and setting the seed directly if > 1."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390092",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "TEST_CASE inside a TEST_SUITE does not run the suite fixture, deviating from Boost and the PR description.",
      "quote": "TEST_SUITE_BEGIN(suite, Fixture) sets btc_suite_fixture, but TEST_CASE registers a plain function and never uses it.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978601459"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3978601459",
      "settled_by_quote": "Seems fine. I would think it very strange to update a global as part of a test fixture, but this is a code reduction and should hopefully simplify review."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:4959035820",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "An in-house test framework allows customizing test runner behavior to Core's needs, unblocking concurrency improvements and removing barriers to writing tests.",
      "substantive": true
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5061768134",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "Test suite passes and the scripted-diff reproduces cleanly.",
      "substantive": true
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Initial record update for PR 35713. All objections from maflcko regarding compile-time static assertions for stringifying and from jeanpablojp regarding test-runner flags, segfault on null cstrings, stdout flushing, seed reproducibility, guix linker flags, and suite fixture invocation were addressed and pushed by the author."
}

participants.note: Strong Concept ACK endorsing in-house customizable test runner
objected to fallback printing type names instead of compile failure on unprintable types (resolved with static assert and CHECK_NO_DISPLAY)
clarified Boost header-only usage and discussed constexpr / inline constexpr sweeps
Concept ACK, but raised multiple behavioral regressions and bug reports (resolved by author pushes)

claims.harm: Silently printing mangled or compile-time type names at runtime instead of failing compilation when formatting is missing loses compile-time safety and differs from master.
claims.quote: This should remain a compile failure, like it is on current master.
claims.settled_by_quote: CHECK_NO_DISPLAY sounds fine. The benefit of the static assert is that it can print the problem and solution at compile time

claims.harm: Dropping BOOST_TEST_RUN_FILTERS causes test coverage scripts to run the whole test suite instead of specific suites, and dropping flags breaks downstream scripts like libmultiprocess CI.
claims.quote: BOOST_TEST_RUN_FILTERS is no longer read, so deterministic-unittest-coverage runs the whole binary instead of the suite it was given.
claims.settled_by_quote: I added a catch_system_error flag for compatibility as well as a separation between the summary and log level.

claims.harm: Comparing null C-strings segfaults rather than reporting a test failure.
claims.quote: With either side null this segfaults instead of reporting the failure.
claims.settled_by_quote: Added a check if either side is null so it does not go through strcmp

claims.harm: Unflushed output causes test logs before a crash to be lost and causes duplicate output on child process exits.
claims.quote: This never flushes. With a crash inside a test case and output redirected, master keeps the preceding lines and here the file comes back empty.
claims.settled_by_quote: I think a cout flush should solve these. Updated in latest push.

claims.harm: Dropping the entire guix linker block drops -Wl,--fatal-warnings from all Linux builds instead of only dropping the riscv64 exception.
claims.quote: Dropping the whole block means no Linux host links with -Wl,--fatal-warnings any more, while build_win.sh and build_win_gui.sh keep it.
claims.settled_by_quote: Added Wl, --fatal-warnings on head commit, lmk if thats what you mean

claims.harm: BOOST_TEST_RANDOM is treated as a boolean without parsing the seed value or logging the used seed, making test run ordering non-reproducible.
claims.quote: Here the value is only checked for presence, never read, so 0 and an empty string both turn shuffling on and a fixed seed no longer reproduces.
claims.settled_by_quote: Fixed by using a random seed and printing it if equal to 1, and setting the seed directly if > 1.

claims.harm: TEST_CASE inside a TEST_SUITE does not run the suite fixture, deviating from Boost and the PR description.
claims.quote: TEST_SUITE_BEGIN(suite, Fixture) sets btc_suite_fixture, but TEST_CASE registers a plain function and never uses it.
claims.settled_by_quote: Seems fine. I would think it very strange to update a global as part of a test fixture, but this is a code reduction and should hopefully simplify review.

support.reason: An in-house test framework allows customizing test runner behavior to Core's needs, unblocking concurrency improvements and removing barriers to writing tests.
Test suite passes and the scripted-diff reproduces cleanly.

result.notes: Initial record update for PR 35713. All objections from maflcko regarding compile-time static assertions for stringifying and from jeanpablojp regarding test-runner flags, segfault on null cstrings, stdout flushing, seed reproducibility, guix linker flags, and suite fixture invocation were addressed and pushed by the author.
